messages.subject: multiple lines plots with different colours
parts:
Dear ggplotters,

I am trying to do a very simple graph but for some reason I get a very messy plot.

My dataset is DFsel where I plot y=year and x=value for the variable age_TFR that has two values 1 and 2. What I want to obtain is two lines of two different colours for all the provinces in the plot (defines in prove_geo), except for a single province that I want to highlight with different colours (Barcelona prov_num=38). When I plot by geo_points there is no problem, but since I want lines the following code gives me a messy vertical lines plot.
Also, how can I plot Barcelona with a different colour of my choice?

p <- ggplot(DFsel, aes(year,value, colour=age_TFR))
p + geom_line() +
labs(title = "Total Period Fertility Rate: Age contribution to total fertility",
x = "", y = "") +
theme(axis.text = element_text(colour="grey", size=8, angle=0,
face = "plain"),
axis.text.x = element_text(hjust=.5, vjust=.7),
axis.text.y = element_text(hjust=1, vjust=0),
strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour =
"black", angle = 0),
plot.title = element_text(size=20),
plot.margin = unit(c(1,1,1,1), "cm")
) +

facet_wrap(~ prov_geo, ncol=6)

I appreciate any help on the matter.

Ale

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: multiple lines plots with different colours
parts:
Ale, 

You may need to use the group option if your lines are connecting is a strange way. Hard to say without a picture or reproducible dataset. If you want to plot one of the sub plots in the facet wrap with a different color, you'll probably need to define the barcelona as a 3rd level of your age_TFR factor, and use scale_colour_manual() to hard code your color to what you want. 

HTH, 

B

messages.subject: Re: multiple lines plots with different colours
parts:
Ale, 

What exactly do you want to visualize with your data? 

The reason you get strangeness is that you have more than one point at each timepoint along your x-axis. 

From your data it looks like you have an interaction between "order" and "age_TFR" that gives you individual "lines". 

ggplot(DFsel, aes(year,value, colour=interaction(order,age_TFR))) + geom_point()+ facet_wrap(~ prov_geoorder, ncol=6)



HTH, 

B

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: multiple lines plots with different colours
parts:
Ale, 

It's best if you don't send the same email to the list multiple times. 

interaction creates a factor with all combinations of two factors. In your case it's order (1,2,11) x age_TFR (1,2) and the combinations are 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 11.1 and 11.2. If this is the output that you want, you may wish to create this factor in your dataframe itself as a new column. 

If all you need to do is rename the legend and the factor levels: 

+ labs(colour="MyNewTitle")+
scale_colour_discrete(labels=c("1.1a", "1.2b", "2.1a", "2.2b", "11.1a", "11.2b"))

As far as "popping" out Barca only... I'm not sure, perhaps others have ideas. 

B

messages.subject: Re: multiple lines plots with different colours
parts:
To separate colors between Barcelona and the other provinces, you need to create an indicator variable for Barcelona. Since you want different colors by age and Barcelona/not Barcelona combinations, the interaction() function can be used. I think the following code does the core of what you asked for, albeit rather crudely. I also thought it would be better to plot the province names rather than the geoorder, so there are a few lines for that purpose.

# Pick out the unique province names and corresponding geoorders,
# then reorder the province names by geoorder
x <- unique(DFsel$prov_name)
y <- unique(DFsel$prov_geoorder)
z <- x[y]

DFsel$age_TFR <- factor(DFsel$age_TFR)
DFsel$order <- factor(DFsel$order, levels = c(1, 2, 11))
DFsel$province <- factor(DFsel$prov_name, levels = z)

# Restrict to order = 11 observations
DFsel11 <- subset(DFsel, order == 11)

# Create the Barcelona indicator and interact it with age_TFR
# The names I chose are ugly - hopefully you can do better.
DFsel11$barca <- DFsel11$prov_name == "Barcelona"
DFsel11$barcage <- with(DFsel11, interaction(barca, age_TFR))
DFsel11$barcage <- factor(DFsel11$barcage, labels = c("~Barcelona1", 
                           " Barcelona1", "~Barcelona2", " Barcelona2"))

ggplot(DFsel11, aes(year, value, colour = barcage)) + 
     geom_line(size = 1) + 
     scale_colour_manual(values = c("orange", "firebrick", "blue", "black")) +
     scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1980, 2000)) +
     labs(x = NULL, y = "", colour = "ageTFR") +
     facet_wrap(~ province, ncol=6) +
     ggtitle("Total Period Fertility Rate: Age contribution to total fertility") +

theme(axis.text    = element_text(colour="grey", size=8, angle=0,
                                      face = "plain"),
           axis.text.x  = element_text(hjust=.5, vjust=.7),
           axis.text.y  = element_text(hjust=1, vjust=0),
           strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour =
                                        "black", angle = 0),
plot.title   = element_text(size = 16),

plot.margin  = unit(c(1,1,1,1), "cm")
          )

You may want to consider putting the legend at the bottom (legend.position = "bottom" in theme()) to provide a bit more horizontal space for the panels.

Dennis
